blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Documentary collections, viewed strategically, are less about a single shipment and more about the overall balance of risk within a trading relationship. At scale, a mature trade team uses collections selectively: on buyers with strong payment history, on routes where logistical risk is low, on commodities where a rejected parcel can easily be resold.

The decision is therefore not collection or LC but which risks am I already carrying, and which risks do I need to transfer? A collection transfers the risk of misaligned documents but not the risk of buyer default. A letter of credit transfers more, at a higher cost. A structured receivables programme — where the bank discounts the draft — can transfer almost all of it, at a still higher cost.

If a finance team had only one instrument, they would face every trade with a hammer. Mature trade businesses carry the whole toolbox and choose deliberately, trade by trade, between simplicity and protection. The quiet art is matching the instrument to the true risk, not to the habit of the team.

items.q: According to the text, what does a documentary collection transfer?
options: The risk of buyer default, but not document risk
Logistical and default risk together
Almost all of the trade's risk
The risk of misaligned documents, but not buyer default
items.why: "A collection transfers the risk of misaligned documents but not the risk of buyer default."

items.q: Why does a receivables programme cost more than an LC?
options: Because it only works on weak buyers
Because the bank discounts the draft and absorbs almost all the risk
Because it requires two banks instead of one
Because it takes longer to arrange
items.why: "A structured receivables programme — where the bank discounts the draft — can transfer almost all of it, at a still higher cost."

items.q: When does the text say a mature team uses collections?
options: On every trade, for the sake of consistency
Selectively — on strong buyers, low-risk routes and resaleable commodities
Only when an LC is unavailable
Only on brand-new trading relationships
items.why: "a mature trade team uses collections selectively: on buyers with strong payment history… low… commodities where a rejected parcel can easily be resold."

items.q: The image of facing "every trade with a hammer" suggests that the author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The right instrument depends on the specific risk of the trade
A team should standardise on one instrument and apply it everywhere
Collections and LCs transfer different kinds of risk
Cost and protection have to be weighed against each other
items.why: Inferência: a metáfora do martelo critica justamente o uso de um só instrumento para tudo.

items.q: The phrase "not to the habit of the team" implies that…
options: habits are the most reliable guide to risk
teams should always default to the cheapest instrument
many teams choose instruments out of routine rather than genuine risk analysis
the finance team should be replaced regularly
items.why: Inferência: o autor contrasta o 'true risk' com o hábito, sugerindo que a escolha por costume é um erro comum.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando a nova política de instrumentos ao time de trade. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, thank you all for coming. What I'm proposing is not a new instrument — it's a new way of choosing between the ones we already have. For years this desk has reached for a collection by default, simply because it's what we know best. From today, I want the question to be different.

Before you pick anything, I want two things written on the deal sheet: which risks am I already comfortable carrying, and which risks genuinely need to move off our book? If the buyer has a ten-year payment history and the cargo is easy to resell, a collection is probably plenty — and it's cheap. But if we're shipping into a new counterparty on a difficult route, I don't want us defaulting to a collection just to save a few basis points.

Here's the part that matters. If we had built this discipline two years ago, we would not be sitting on the exposure we're carrying today. So the receivables programme is now on the table for the larger flows — yes, the bank takes a bigger cut, but it takes almost all the default risk with it. Match the instrument to the real risk of the trade, please, not to the habit of this desk.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Emily actually proposing?
options: That the desk stop using collections entirely
That every trade now use a receivables programme
A new way of choosing between the instruments the desk already has
A brand-new financial instrument
items.why: "it's not a new instrument — it's a new way of choosing between the ones we already have."

items.q: What two questions does Emily want written on the deal sheet?
options: The buyer's credit rating and the cargo value
The margin target and the delivery date
Which risks are already comfortable to carry, and which need to move off the book
The bank's fee and the shipping route
items.why: "which risks am I already comfortable carrying, and which risks genuinely need to move off our book?"

items.q: For a ten-year buyer with easily resaleable cargo, what does Emily say is appropriate?
options: No instrument at all
A receivables programme, to be safe
A letter of credit, because it transfers the most risk
A collection, which is probably plenty and cheap
items.why: "a collection is probably plenty — and it's cheap."

items.q: When Emily says "If we had built this discipline two years ago, we would not be sitting on the exposure we're carrying today," she is implying that…
options: the current exposure is at least partly the result of past habits
the bank is responsible for the current risk
the desk has never carried any exposure
the discipline will take another two years to work
items.why: Inferência (mixed conditional): a falta de disciplina no passado explica a exposição atual.

items.q: Why is Emily wary of "defaulting to a collection just to save a few basis points"?
options: Because collections are always the most expensive option
Because the bank forbids collections on new routes
Because basis points are impossible to measure
Because on a risky new counterparty the small saving is not worth the extra default risk
items.why: Inferência: em rota difícil com contraparte nova, economizar pouco não compensa o risco de calote assumido.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The whole point of a collection is risk transfer — moving exposure off our own book." Risk transfer means…
options: shifting a given risk to another party
delaying a payment deadline
insuring the physical cargo only
calculating the total value of a trade
items.why: Risk transfer = transferência de risco: passar a exposição para outra parte (banco, contraparte).

items.q: Choose the correct term: "On buyers with a strong ___, a simple collection is usually enough."
options: payment history
draft
hammer
toolbox
items.why: Payment history = histórico de pagamento — o que qualifica o comprador para o instrumento mais leve.

items.q: "A mature trade team carries the whole toolbox." Here mature describes a team that is…
options: experienced and disciplined in its choices
close to retirement age
the oldest desk in the bank
reluctant to change
items.why: Mature = maduro: no contexto, experiente e criterioso, não uma questão de idade literal.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Under the receivables programme the bank will ___ the draft, paying us early for a fee."
options: discount
resell
endorse
reject
items.why: To discount (the draft) = descontar o saque: adiantar o valor cobrando uma taxa.

items.q: "We should choose instruments deliberately, trade by trade." Deliberately means…
options: reluctantly
in secret
on purpose, with careful thought
quickly and by instinct
items.why: Deliberately = deliberadamente: de forma consciente e ponderada, o oposto de agir por hábito.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de trade finance. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Treasury still has to sign off on the receivables programme before we roll it out." To sign off on means to…
options: question informally
formally approve
postpone indefinitely
audit afterwards
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new selection policy on the larger flows first." To roll out means to…
options: test in secret
outsource to the bank
implement in stages
quietly cancel
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two traders pushed back on dropping the default collection." They…
options: approved it at once
rewrote the policy themselves
resisted or objected to it
forgot about it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar por completo.

items.q: "The desk agreed the risk-based approach but never followed through." They…
options: delegated it to the bank
documented it in detail
carried it out fully
failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto aconteceu.

items.q: "Shaving a few basis points off the fee won't move the needle on our overall exposure." This means it will…
options: trigger an audit
not make a noticeable difference
double the cost
cause immediate resistance
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, a economia é pequena demais para isso.
